bullets.title: S&P bounces ~1.2% but VIX still elevated at 25.48 — rally seen as limited
bullets.body: S&P 500 futures up ~1.5% to 7,305 Friday morning with the index closing +1.2% to 7,271 Thursday; semis (SOXX +4%) led the bounce. 22V and others see the rally as limited — a re-test of ~7,600 would offset gains via higher UST yields/stronger USD, and the market is likely range-bound until core PCE tracks meaningfully toward 2%. VIX at 25.48 (+9.9%) reflects lingering uncertainty despite the risk-on tape.

bullets.title: Q3 GDP revised to 4.3%, PCE at 3.8% — Fed stays hawkish, 2% target still distant
bullets.body: Q3 GDP was revised up to 4.3% (from 3.5%), with just over half the upside attributable to AI-related IP and data center investment. October PCE came in at 3.8% YoY and nominal GDP is running ~6.3%, requiring a 21bp/month core PCE decline to hit the Fed's 2027 target. 22V and PSC Macro (Nancy Lazar) both flag sticky inflation diffusion and expect Fed to remain hawkish, with financial conditions already tightening meaningfully.

bullets.title: October goods deficit widens to record $149.5bn on capex-led import surge — 4Q GDP drag risk
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley: the goods trade deficit hit $149.5bn in October, the widest since 2022 outside tariff front-running periods. Real capital goods imports ex-autos surged 7.4% m/m and +65% y/y; if sustained, net exports would be a meaningful drag on 4Q GDP. JPMorgan's capex nowcaster for 4Q26 is tracking at 9.4% annualized (up 40bps w/w), with EM ex-China at 17.3%.

bullets.title: AI adoption early-stage (10-20% workplace), compute demand ~5x supply — structural capex case intact
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs European AI & Semis Symposium found workplace AI usage at just 10-20% and only 2.2% of US households have paid AI subscriptions, underscoring how early-stage adoption remains. Compute demand is estimated at ~5x available supply, supporting elevated GPU rental rates, and the shift toward inference from training is constructive for managed compute platforms. Sovereign AI and regulatory constraints on datacenter builds add complexity to the deployment picture.

bullets.title: Semis momentum unwind may be bottoming — Dec 2018 analog cited, but memory lagging signals weak conviction
bullets.body: The semiconductor sector rallied 8% intraday Wednesday from lows (NASDAQ +4.2%) in a move compared to the Dec 2018 inflection. However, memory stocks (MU -15%, SNDK -24% over 5 days) acted worst in the reversal, closing -5% vs. semis +8%, indicating limited real buyer conviction; NAND/DRAM spot pricing continues to decline m/m on non-AI demand weakness. Hedge funds are reportedly using memory as a funding short against other longs.

bullets.title: AI momentum factor unwind: Tech Hardware -35%, Semis -14% MTD; EPS-Mo/Price-Mo swap up 20%
bullets.body: 22V quant: Technology accounted for -4.7pp of S&P 1500's -5.3% November decline, with Tech Hardware and Semis momentum baskets down 35.1% and 14.4% MTD respectively. Short-term volatility in Price Momentum hit the 93rd percentile — rarely seen outside recessions. The recommended long-EPS Momentum / short-Price Momentum swap has gained 20.2% since late-June, and 22V advocates blending Value and Momentum to temper volatility.

bullets.title: NVDA/China Blackwell smuggling report adds geopolitical overhang ahead of Jensen Congressional testimony
bullets.body: Reports of Blackwell chips found in a Shanghai data center and an ongoing GPU investigation into SE Asia distribution channels briefly softened E-Mini futures Friday morning. Jensen Huang is scheduled to testify before Congress next week; the Trump administration is seen as supportive, but testimony outcome is uncertain. Dutch government resistance to US Match Act export controls on ASML litho tools is a separate but related risk — ASML derives ~23% of systems revenue from China.

bullets.title: China equity stabilization measures underwhelm — CSI 300 still -19.7% from peak despite Friday's 4.2% pop
bullets.body: 22V Research: State Council signaled stepped-up capital market support, sending the CSI 300 up 4.2% and the STAR 50 tech index up 15% on Friday, but the CSI 300 remains down 19.7% from its June peak. The current toolkit relies on existing measures (national team buying, buybacks) without major new fiscal stimulus; the STAR 50 trades at a trailing P/E of 100. Key December policy meetings (Politburo early Dec, CEWC Dec 8-16) are unlikely to signal a major shift.

bullets.title: Data center power demand surges: Applied Digital signs 150MW 18-year lease, $41B+ contracted revenue
bullets.body: Applied Digital secured a 150MW, 18-year lease with an investment-grade hyperscaler, pushing total contracted revenue above $41B. FCC authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1M satellites for orbital data centers through 2040. Municipal permitting delays (Aurora through Sept 2027, Bloomington extended 2 years) and Cogent's data center asset sales at $6M/MW vs. a $10M/MW initial target highlight valuation complexity in the sector.

bullets.title: France flirting with recession: 3Q GDP -1.0% q/q saar, fiscal deficit at 5.4% of GDP with political risk
bullets.body: France's 3Q26 GDP was revised down sharply to -1.0% q/q saar (from -0.5%), with 1Q and 2Q also downgraded, showing contraction across all three quarters. Household investment collapsed -7.3% q/q saar and construction output is declining for a third consecutive quarter; the general government deficit sits at 5.4% of GDP. Political uncertainty is elevated with Le Pen leading runoff polls and the government lacking a parliamentary majority for the 2027 budget.

bullets.title: UK inflation to peak above 4% in H1 2027 — JPMorgan forecasts two more BoE hikes to 4.5%
bullets.body: JPMorgan forecasts CPI will peak above 4% in H1 2027 due to an energy shock, with the BoE hiking twice more (February and April) to 4.5% by Q2 2027. November PMI fell to 52.3, with the employment sub-index at 48.5 pulling down the Q4 nowcast to 0.5%. Fiscal tightening is expected to contribute a 0.5% drag on 2027 growth.

bullets.title: BofA cuts Brazil to marketweight, upgrades Mexico; LatAm easing cycle delayed by sticky inflation
bullets.body: BofA downgraded Brazil equities from overweight to marketweight and upgraded Mexico to marketweight for 2027, citing Brazil's projected growth of just 0.3% and a primary surplus requirement of ~3.0% of GDP to stabilize debt vs. a -0.3% estimate for 2026. Brazil non-performing loans hit a record 5.1% with household delinquency at 6.1%; the BCB is not expected to resume cutting rates until 4Q27. BofA targets Ibov 190k and Mexbol 80k for 2027.

bullets.title: Global 2027 outlook: BofA hawkish on Fed/BoJ/BoE, dovish ECB; Brent at $80, gold constructive
bullets.body: BofA's 2027 macro framework expects global growth to slip to 3.4% from 3.5%. The house is hawkish on Fed, BoJ, and BoE but dovish on the ECB; copper is expected to rally on a China rebound, gold outlook is constructive on reduced external war risk, and Brent oil is forecast at $80/bbl with European TTF gas averaging €55/MWh.

bullets.title: Mexico trade balance flips to $298M surplus on record tech exports — potential structural shift
bullets.body: Mexico's October trade balance swung from a $606M deficit to a $298M surplus as tech exports hit an all-time high, driving total exports to a record $86bn (+30.2% y/y). Non-auto manufacturing exports surged 8.4% seasonally adjusted; analysts flag this may represent a structural shift to persistently smaller deficits, though normalization is expected in 2027 as tech CAPEX moderates and base effects diminish.

bullets.title: US retail credit/debit spending decelerated to +1.6% w/w (Nov 22) — below 6-week avg of +2.1%
bullets.body: KeyBanc First Look data shows all-retail spending growth slowed to +1.6% for the week of November 22, below the prior week's +2.5% and the six-week average of +2.1%. The trend is a step-down from October's +2.8% and September's +4.0%, pointing to deceleration heading into the holiday season.

bullets.title: Precious metals and base metals broadly bid — elevated call activity, gold constructive across desks
bullets.body: Canadian markets rallied with the TSX Composite +1.43%; precious metals led with names up 3.1-12.2% and base metals (NCX +9.3%, PNPN +8.5%) also surging. Unusual options activity flagged elevated call volume in precious metals names (B, HBM, HYMC). BofA's 2027 view is constructive on gold given reduced geopolitical tail risk.

bullets.title: Housing data mixed: new home sales surge to 701K (highest since Dec 2025), but existing sales -8.8% y/y
bullets.body: UBS mortgage finance data shows new home sales rose 14.2% to 701,000 units in October, the highest reading since December 2025, while existing home sales fell 5.5% m/m and 8.8% y/y. MBS spreads widened modestly to 129bps vs. USTs; the 30-year fixed mortgage rate eased slightly to 7.21%. CMBS special servicing hit 11.74% with office delinquencies up 17bps to 12.33%.

bullets.title: WTI +1.3% to $85.28 as OPEC+ meets Sunday; energy mixed in Canadian session
bullets.body: WTI crude is up 1.3% to $85.28, supported by Middle East activity and the broader market rebound ahead of an OPEC+ meeting Sunday to discuss output targets. Energy names in Canada were mixed (EOG +4.6%, TCW +2.0%) while Brent is forecast at $80/bbl for 2027 by BofA.

bullets.title: 10-year yield up 4bps to 4.90% — higher UST rates remain the key cap on equity upside
bullets.body: The 10-year Treasury yield ticked up 4bps to 4.90% Friday morning alongside the equity rally, reinforcing 22V's view that any meaningful S&P re-rating above ~7,600 would be self-limiting as higher yields tighten financial conditions. The bonds-equities correlation remains deeply negative and financial conditions have already tightened materially.

bullets.title: JPM 4Q26 capex nowcaster at 9.4% annualized; capital goods exports tracking jumped +6.5pp w/w
bullets.body: JPMorgan's global capex nowcast for 4Q26 is running at 9.4% saar (up 0.4pp from prior week), with the investment goods PMI elevated at 53.2. Capital goods exports tracking improved sharply, +6.5pp w/w to 21.6% for 4Q26. Developed markets are tracking at 10.2% and EM ex-China at 17.3%, consistent with the capex-led import surge seen in October trade data.
